svg.text: Fluorescence polarisation: how binding is read out
Photoselection: the vertical field excites only molecules
whose dipole happens to lie along z —
that is why the emission starts out polarised
collected along y, toward the viewer
one polariser, turned between the readings
direction of the emission dipole during the ~4 ns excited state
faster than the lifetime → it turns several times before emitting
aptamer on the virus — one big, slow object
direction of the emission dipole during the ~4 ns excited state
slower than the lifetime → it barely turns before emitting
G corrects the detector's own polarisation bias
